      "result": "inconclusive",
      "replication_type": "close extension",
      "original_url": "https://doi.org/10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001232",
      "original_title": "Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain",
      "original_authors": "Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean",
      "original_year": "2018",
      "original_journal": "Pain",
      "description": "Martucci et al. (2018) reported that patients with fibromyalgia showed reduced medial prefrontal cortex responses during anticipation of monetary gains compared with healthy controls.",
      "citation_sentence": "A previous study by Martucci et al. (2018) combining fMRI with the MID task found that brain responses to monetary reward are altered in patients with fibromyalgia.",
      "gt_ambiguity": "clear",
      "notes": "The replication found the same-direction reduction as a non-significant trend, and the authors described the result as generally consistent but not fully replicated."
    },
    {
      "result": "inconclusive",
      "replication_type": "close extension",
      "original_url": "https://doi.org/10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001232",
      "original_title": "Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain",
      "original_authors": "Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean",
      "original_year": "2018",
      "original_journal": "Pain",
      "description": "Martucci et al. (2018) reported that patients with fibromyalgia showed enhanced medial prefrontal cortex responses to non-punishment monetary outcomes compared with healthy controls.",
      "citation_sentence": "Compared to healthy controls, patients demonstrated reduced MPFC responses during the anticipation of reward gains, but enhanced MPFC responses in response to non-punishment outcomes.",
      "gt_ambiguity": "clear",
      "notes": "The replication found the same-direction increase as a non-significant trend, which the authors treated as a generally similar but incomplete replication."
    },
    {
      "result": "success",
      "replication_type": "close extension",
      "original_url": "https://doi.org/10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001232",
      "original_title": "Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain",
      "original_authors": "Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean",
      "original_year": "2018",
      "original_journal": "Pain",
      "description": "Martucci et al. (2018) reported no difference between patients with fibromyalgia and healthy controls in nucleus accumbens response during anticipation of monetary gains.",
      "citation_sentence": "NAcc responses during the anticipation of reward gains, however, did not significantly differ between patients vs. controls (Martucci et al., 2018).",
      "gt_ambiguity": "clear",
      "notes": "This was an original null claim, and the replication also found no patient-control difference; the authors explicitly described the result as consistent."
    },
    {
      "result": "success",
      "replication_type": "close extension",
      "original_url": "https://doi.org/10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001232",
      "original_title": "Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain",
      "original_authors": "Martucci, Katherine; Borg, Nick; Macniven, Kim; Knutson, Brian; Mackey, Sean",
      "original_year": "2018",
      "original_journal": "Pain",
      "description": "Martucci et al. (2018) reported that greater medial prefrontal cortex response to non-punishment outcomes was associated with greater mood disturbance.",
      "citation_sentence": "These analyses suggested that across both studies, MPFC response to non-punishment outcome was positively correlated with individual differences in mood disturbance (i.e., greater MPFC response was related to higher mood disturbance as indicated by higher self-reported POMS scores).",
      "gt_ambiguity": "clear",
      "notes": "The replication reproduced the positive association, although the within-group association was primarily driven by the fibromyalgia group."
    }
  ]
}
